name.en: どんぐりころころ (Donguri Korokoro)

licence.attribution: どんぐりころころ (Donguri Korokoro). Words: 青木存義 Aoki Nagayoshi (1935). Music: 梁田貞 Yanada Tadashi (1959). First published 1921 or 1922. Public domain in Japan and the United States.

_licence.source: ja.wikisource どんぐりころころ

japan.basis: lyricist 青木存義 Aoki Nagayoshi (1935); composer 梁田貞 Yanada Tadashi (1959). The later of the two deaths is 1959.
japan.test: Japan: both authors died 1967 or earlier, or the work is anonymous and published 1967 or earlier.

us.test: US: published 1930 or earlier, or published later with every author dead in 1945 or earlier, because the URAA restored anything still protected in its source country on 1996-01-01.

_licence.confidence_text: High. ja.wikipedia states outright that both terms expired and the work is public domain. Verses 1 and 2 only: an editorial note says the third verse is not public domain.
_licence.verses_permitted_note: Two, and the reason is copyright, not transcription. The third verse of this song is not public domain, per the editorial note on its ja.wikipedia article. It must never be added to this file.
_licence.note: Derived from data/songs/donguri-korokoro.json: one item per line, the pieces cut on the word boundaries of the corpus's romaji line aligned onto the kana (a one-kana piece joins the piece before it, a repeated piece is one piece), the verse gloss shown after a miss. Verdicts, credits and the authors' death years are copied from that file. Qualifier: verses 1 and 2 only.

items.line: どんぐり ころころ どんぶりこ

gloss.en: An acorn rolls along and plop, into the pond: what a to-do. A loach comes up and says hello, young master, let us play together.

items.line: どんぐり ころころ よろこんで

gloss.en: The acorn was delighted and played a while, but it missed the hillside after all, and its crying troubled the loach.
